title: Nellie's Happy Stamp Day
markdown:
The sun stretched its fingers through the post-office windows and woke Nellie the otter. Today felt special. She hurried to her stamping station, where neat parcels waited in a queue that knew its manners. Her job was to stamp them. Today: a tiny acorn stamper. “This will make the most cheerful marks,” she whispered, as if the acorn had asked for a review.

Miss Eaves, the postmistress, bustled in. “Good morning. A busy day?”

“The busiest. And the most exciting.” A giggle, then a big parcel for Willow Creek. Nellie dipped the acorn in sparkly blue ink and pressed. The acorn wobbled. Instead of a star, a dazzling swirly pattern popped onto the brown paper, twinkling like a pocket of night sky that had sat down.

“Oh my.”

Miss Eaves peered. “Quite a stamp. Grand. A tiny piece of the night sky.”

Plink. The parcel zipped off. Soon a message arrived from Willow Creek: the sender had loved the swirly star. The most glamorous stamp they had ever seen. It had made the whole day shine.

Word spread. Parcels arrived from everywhere asking for a stamp like Willow Creek’s, a glamorous one too. Nellie’s paws worked at happy speed: swooping swirls, shimmering dots, glittering lines.

Bram the rook flapped in. “I can peck out extra details!” His quick pecks added tiny dots that looked like they had been invited.

“This is a bit tricky,” Nellie admitted. One stamp became a funny smudge. Parcels piled. Miss Eaves watched, kind eyes thoughtful.

“The excitement is a pleasure. The parcels are getting delayed.” She tapped a tall stack. “Perhaps a little contest.”

Nellie’s ears perked. “A contest?”

“A Happy Stamp Contest. Prize for the most creative picture that brings the most genuine joy.”

Nellie thought of the Willow Creek flutter, then of the waiting stack. A simple sun bloomed as an idea. “A bright cheerful sun. Everyone loves a sunny day.”

She dipped the acorn in sunshine-yellow ink. Pop. With control and a heart full of purpose she stamped a beaming sun on each parcel. Townsfolk saw the cheerful marks, smiled, clapped. A simple sun, stamped with delight, did the work the night-sky swirl had started, and the queue began to move again.

Nellie beamed. The office was busy and filled with gentle cheer. She did not declare the day a marvel of the age. She logged wobble-swirl / Willow Creek message / yellow sun in the post book, left Bram a corner of dots to peck if he wished, and let Miss Eaves start the next pile while the acorn, for once, sat still.
